analysis.title: Early Morning Reid – Macro Strategy
key_insights: Tech sentiment turned cautious overnight. Alphabet fell almost 10% after hours on Google Services revenue of $96.3bn vs $98.4bn est. Ad revenue grew at its slowest pace in five quarters, which renewed doubts that AI capex will pay off fast enough.

Samsung Electronics is down about 5% in Asia. Its chip unit's operating profit missed analyst expectations and it delayed its new shareholder return plan. KOSPI is down 1.20%, after being down about 3% earlier.

Microsoft gained about 3% in extended trading on cloud revenue growth of +48% yoy vs +44% est. That was not enough to lift the tech mood. Nasdaq futures are down 1.20% and S&P 500 futures are down 0.35%.

Yesterday the S&P 500 rose 0.28% to close within 1% of its record high. The Philly semiconductor index rose 1.75%, led by Oracle (+10.73%) after it projected a return to positive free cash flow, and CoreWeave (+7.32%). The broader Nasdaq rose only 0.27%.

The FOMC held the fed funds rate at 3.75-4.00% with two dissents, Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack, both for a 25bp hike. The statement upgraded activity from solid to strong. Chair Warsh said he is unable and unwilling to call financial conditions tight and gave no forward guidance.

Deutsche Bank economists still expect 25bp Fed hikes in December and March. Markets pared back hike pricing after the press conference. December hike odds fell from 91% to 84% and 71bps of tightening is priced by next September, after pricing three hikes going into the meeting.
The Treasury curve steepened. The 2yr yield fell 4.0bps to 4.70% and the 10yr rose 2.0bps to 5.00%. The steeper curve weighed on the dollar, and the euro recovered from a 17-month low.

Warsh outlined an FOMC schedule change. In 2027 one of the eight meetings becomes a strategy discussion and seven stay as policy meetings. In 2028 this moves to six policy meetings and two strategy meetings.

The ECB decision is today and is widely expected to hold. Virtually nothing is priced for today, but a hike is 89% priced by December. Deutsche Bank's baseline is a final hike to 2.75% in December, with some risk of another to 3% in early 2027. Today's focus is communications, with room for a balanced tone because yields and financial conditions have tightened.

European front-month natural gas settled above EUR 100/MWh for the first time since the 2022 energy crisis, up 4.85% to EUR 100.72/MWh and more than 35% so far this month. Storage is historically low, but the refilling outlook has not worsened, so the author sees a risk premium that may be overdone. The 1yr euro inflation swap rose 5.3bps to 3.88%, a joint high since 2023.

Brent settled 1.26% higher at $115.32/bbl but is down about 1.15% this morning after a WSJ report that VP Vance is engaging Iran's Mohsen Rezaei to revive peace talks. Trump downplayed the report as medical-supply outreach. AP reports US officials told allies to prepare for renewed military action against Iran after next week's midterms.

The Israeli shekel fell 2.06%, the worst major currency yesterday. Netanyahu's bloc has a slight edge in Tuesday's election but there is no clear path to a governing majority, so coalition building, a unity government or fresh elections are possible.

UK budget: an additional 2pp tax on property and savings income from April, a bank tax rise from 3% to 6% for 15 months (smaller than expected), and fiscal headroom lowered to £15bn in 2029-30. Deutsche Bank economists see the net impact as marginal. Gilts outperformed and the 10yr yield fell 2.5bps to 5.32%.
The Bank of Canada hiked 25bps to 2.50% as expected and said it could need to raise further but will proceed carefully. Canada's 2yr yield rose 4.0bps and money markets price another hike by January.

Today's calendar covers the ECB decision, US Q3 GDP, September PCE and Eurozone October economic confidence. Amazon, Intel and Blue Owl report earnings. The US auctions $44bn of 7yr Notes and the EU-Canada summit starts.

European credit spreads tightened after their recent sell-off, with IG down 4bps and HY down 16bps. European equities were flat on rising energy costs, with the Stoxx 600 up 0.07% and Spain's IBEX down 1.45%.

tension_points.bear_case: Alphabet's ad revenue grew at its slowest pace in five quarters, raising questions about whether payoffs come fast enough to justify soaring capex. Samsung's chip profit also missed.
